week.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
week.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. new.description: Xbox Series compatibility layer for Windows - runs console game code natively, reimplements the console system libraries and recompiles RDNA2 shaders to DXIL
new.readme: XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (kernelx.dll, XGameRuntime, d3d12xs.dll, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL).

All efforts are scored on one ladder, and a scout refreshes the data every 3 hours. One headline progress bar shows the closest effort, with the top projects pinned to it. new.description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.
new.readme: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow. Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of target/. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. fast-anything finds those functions, has your coding agent port only them to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible. Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain (rustup). --agent takes claude, codex, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin.

new.description: XNU as a loadable kernel module inside Linux (macOS personality for arm64 Linux)
new.readme: Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it. xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel module (xnu.ko) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (fki.ko).

new.description: A continuation of Leonida, the Xbox > PC port interface for GTA VI
new.readme: Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy. Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game.

It translates selected x64 machine code into C++ and selected gfx1013 shaders into desktop DXIL. You can run the public tests without a game installation. Follow the project or ask a question. Start in #start-here on Discord. Read #announcements for verified progress or ask in #general. Everyone is welcome to follow along. For a build problem that others may hit, post the commit, command and error in Development Q&A.

new.description: make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor
new.readme: Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk. There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click. NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger. One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used. Watch the demo on X, with the sound on. Space skips a part. q or Ctrl-C goes to the end.

new.description: A short Lean 4 proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
new.readme: Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions. A Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proof is based on Levent Alpöge's, with Claude (https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf). This repository is a shorter version, produced in collaboration with my colleagues at Anthropic, and Claude. grh/: readable edition, about 300,000 lines. Start at grh/GUIDE.md.

items.lead: Aleph Alpha's Kolibri 1.1 targets faster 1M-context decoding per GPU.
items.body: Teams can now run an open text-generation model with YASA sparse attention claiming up to 14x decode throughput at 1M context. For builders with document-heavy workloads, that speedup would cut serving costs per GPU. Aleph Alpha self-reports the 14x figure, with no accuracy benchmarks or license listed.

items.lead: OpenAI's gpt-live-1.1 crosses a practical threshold for production voice agents.
items.body: Builders can now call this full-duplex API model at $0.05 per active minute, ranking #1 on Jarvis Bench with 100% task completion when delegating to GPT 6.2 Sol Medium. Pairing #1 naturalness, delegated success, and clear pricing gives buyers a production baseline. Results rely on 2,442 Voice Arena votes and leave custom enterprise tools and noisy telephony unproven.

items.lead: New evaluation research clarifies leaderboard noise and cross-platform agent gaps.
items.body: Vernier lets evaluators find the smallest reliable score gap on zero-shot time-series forecasting leaderboards, while OS-Omni tests computer-use agents on live long-horizon workflows across six platforms. Buyers avoid noisy rank shifts, and builders see agents still trail humans on iOS and macOS. Neither supplies public code yet: Vernier includes only a summary without dataset details, and OS-Omni lacks a public harness repo or per-model scores.
